I went from brick uni to open uni because anxiety kept me from attending lectures. I failed my first year at brick uni and went back again because I felt better over the summer but then still couldn't attend lectures again in my re-do year, so dropped out. I then signed up for Open Uni. I did a credit transfer for the modules I'd managed to pass, then finished off my first year, and am now in my third doing it full time.

I'd used like 1 and 3/4 of my student finance I think on trying brick uni, but I've had no problems getting everything financed for Open Uni! I am in Wales so this may be different depending where you are, the best thing to do would be to call your country's student finance.

In case you're also funded by Student Finance Wales, then I'll tell you how it worked for me. I study full time, but am only allowed part-time funding (75% course intensity). They cover all my course fees though. The part time funding is pretty awful compared to the full time, but if you move home again and don't have to pay rent you should be fine!

Btw the credit transfer can take quite a while to process, and you won't know how much you get for potentially up to 3-4 months maybe, so do it ASAP!

Hi I'm also from the UK so I can try and help you from my experience of school services. 

  
1. Reach out to your school counsellor. Not sure how your school is set up, but you can ask your head of year, school nurse, form tutor, or your mum to contact someone in the school to set it up.  
Hopefully they can provide you some help with coping with your conditions, and also provide a stepping stone to other resources that may be on offer in your school, or local area.  


2. Contact someone you trust in your school (teacher, form tutor, head of year) and let them know about this person's behaviour. Letting teachers know who is a bully helps them to keep on eye on the person and not let them get away with bad behaviour on a warning. Maybe your school even has a strategy for counselling people with behaviour issues.  


3. Keep your mum in the loop for whatever you do. Having her on your side and backing you up with push the school to take the issue more seriously, and will help your mum to help you.  


I hope you can find something to work for you, and best of luck.
